clock_time_reference: The Democracy Clock held at 7:41 p.m. for the second consecutive week, moving only one tenth of a minute internally. This near-stillness reflects a week of very high coercive activity offset by court and civic resistance strong enough to blunt but not reverse the trend.

grand_total_points.note: The net public clock movement was a mere one tenth of a minute, masking a much larger volume of internal trait-level activity that mostly offset itself.

delta_summary.moral_floor: The moral floor eroded further this week, with serious breaches in character, ethics, and truthfulness only partially offset by judicial rulings and organized civic resistance.
delta_summary.net_interpretation: Despite the calm surface reading, Week 22 represented a deepening and confident repetition of prior authoritarian patterns rather than a new escalation, with accountability mechanisms functioning but consistently outpaced by the speed and volume of executive action.

traits_moved.note: Twenty-two traits registered measurable movement this week, reflecting broad but individually modest shifts across immigration, oversight, media, and economic capture domains.

long_synopsis: Week 22 saw no single rupture, but a flood of coercive activity that outpaced institutional response. The administration directed ICE to target Democratic-run cities by name, deployed troops to Los Angeles, and reversed a brief pause on workplace raids. An Oregon vineyard manager was detained, protected-area guidance for schools and churches was withdrawn, and journalist Mario Guevara was arrested and transferred to ICE custody. Nationwide No Kings protests drew massive crowds, met by tear gas, prosecutions, and a Florida official's suggestion that drivers could run over demonstrators. Courts blocked some actions, including unlawful NIH grant terminations and passport restrictions, but appellate rulings also preserved federal troop control pending appeal. The EPA dropped an enforcement case against a major Trump donor, crypto oversight loosened, and Voice of America lost 639 employees. The public clock barely moved, concealing a widening gap between accountability and executive speed.
short_synopsis: Immigration raids, military deployment, and protests collided this week as federal power targeted opposition cities while courts, journalists, and civil society pushed back with uneven success. The clock barely moved, masking a week of dense, confident consolidation.

subtitle: A week of raids, parades, and rulings arrived in overwhelming volume, letting old patterns deepen while institutions struggled to answer any single front.
tagline: When power multiplies its fronts faster than institutions can answer any one of them, fragmentation itself becomes a kind of shelter.
title: Fragmentation as Shelter for Power
